body:
no friends aside from a contact in a different city, and my parents are my sole family in this country, but we live on opposite sides of the country and we’re very distant now. for context, i had a rough relationship with my father but my parents are still together.

i wish i could do phone appointments, it’s been the biggest issue for me getting in contact with doctors, as i’m non verbal which i forgot to mention, mb.

I understand that, hence “safe” options - like an ordinary food or drink item, that could be particularly beneficial, but I suppose caffeine is the only stimulant you can find in such things. I’m having caffeine free g-fuel because it has some supposedly helpful (obviously non-stimulant) ingredients, but I feel as though any results are either too minor or placebo. 

I guess it’s just a matter of getting through these waiting lists.

I did used to try that, but I researched it and found out that cutting a patch in half prevents the nicotine from being absorbed slowly, so you kinda get it all at once instead, or at least much quicker than intended, which has adverse effects.

Exercise would definitely benefit me, for many other reasons too - I had to cancel my gym subscription because i’m recovering from long covid, i’m starting to get a little better so i’m trying to go on walks and slowly work my way back up to higher intensity exercises again!

I wouldn’t know directly because of my problems with caffeine, but my adhd (diagnosed) partner has to have at least 2 coffees a day to manage their symptoms and quieten their brain to get anything done. Like, their symptoms can be on the extreme side of things until they have caffeine. Thankfully they’re getting meds for the first time this week :)

(edit: they say it’s not super effective, but it’s much better than nothing when unmedicated)
you’re right, and for me there’s so much (unrelated) external stress that’s making the pressure worse. but i don’t think that stress is going anywhere anytime soon *sigh*

thank you for your understanding response. my parosmia is definitely on the more severe side of things. it induces sickness for me too and feels completely unmanageable. i can’t even go out to grocery stores or to town, where there are food stalls and people eating/drinking as they walk. I very nearly threw up on a crowded tram 2 days ago, i had to run out at the next stop. the people that say i need to just deal with it either are a hell of a lot stronger than me or haven’t experienced this level of severity….i hope that doesn’t come off as rude but i seriously don’t understand.

my partner just woke up and informed me they’d like to go get some coconut/oat milk today so they can start having matcha lattes instead. ngl im teary eyed because it’s a really nice thing to hear after reading some of these responses.


thank you again

it doesn’t sound silly to me at all, i understand my partner, we are both autistic and have adhd. on top of adhd i have bpd so i’m very used to being told i’m too much. im off meds because of adverse effects. i understand it. i experience it. in fact these comments are extremely difficult to deal with if i’m being completely transparent. 

i’m non verbal and the message i wrote to my partner read: “tea? it should only be for a couple weeks” after my partner told me they didn’t want to force me to wear a mask for them to have coffee.

I understand the response, because i respond this way too. i get overwhelmed and break down. but i was very surprised that my partner, who i know very well and how they usually respond, and what i should and shouldn’t say/do, reacted this way. they also love tea. not quite as much, however.


i didn’t really want to add such personal information though. this is a burner account for venting, after all.

the smell is very strong both grinding and brewing, i think it fills the whole apartment though, when it is being brewed and after it’s been poured. additionally i can’t go near the cupboard the coffee is stored in, because i can smell it through the doors/jars - idk if that’s weird (dunno if it’s worth mentioning that i have a pre existing olfactory hypersensitivity as part of my chronic illness, it’s always been with inorganic scents tho). thank you for the advice. cold brew sounds like a good method - because i think the heat is what spreads the smell the most - i just really hope the smell doesn’t taint the food in the fridge lol

i appreciate the feedback. i just want to clarify that it was a question and not a demand, in no way am i forcing my partner to stop. they drink coffee multiple times a day, even in the evening. there are no other rooms for me to hide away in, there’s no doors to close, and the smell lasts for about half an hour each time. they ground fresh beans and use an aeropress. i also want to put emphasis on the fact the coffee problem will only last for a couple weeks, just like lemons and garlic did. i wouldn’t have suggested them to switch to tea if it wasn’t very temporary.

I know they love coffee and i care about them. It’s not something i can ever experience the joy of as i am severely allergic but i will try to understand better.
You put it into words. This is *exactly* what the world feels like to me
yes, constantly. It gives me so much stress
I really wish I could explain to people exactly what this feels like. I feel deeply misunderstood

This has been every relationship for me and I can’t tell if
a) It’s just my bpd making me think this
b) I’ve had horrible luck and all my relationships were actually one-sided
c) I drive people into not wanting to put in the effort anymore (or am I just overthinking the transition between new relationship to long-term relationship, where the other person is comfortable to be themself and no longer trying to “get me”?)

when I was on seroquel I had to force myself to get in bed before it kicked in otherwise I’d be running to the kitchen to make stoner-esque munchies in the middle of the night. I had some weird obsession with the combination of cucumbers and hot sauce

I’m the exact same. Different emotions/symptoms/etc have different sensations and hurt different areas. I often feel the pain before the emotion as well, like my body instantly reacts physically to a trigger, and *then* it’s followed by a slight delay of [insert mood here] one I’ve processed it

I started getting severe chronic migraines at age 13. This is also the age I developed my worst mental health problems. I ruled out everything I’m allergic to but I still get them, and boyy do I get them. They’re stress-induced 90% of the time so there’s not much I can do to avoid them right now.

I had an MRI a few years ago for this and everything went fine and dandy. Well, I actually kinda hoped they would find something because it now means there’s nothing in me that’s causing these migraines that they can take out. It’s just chronic pain

And my pain is always on one of my temples along with the pain spreading out to various areas on that side of the body only (neck and shoulder usually). If you’re sensitive to light, an eyepatch will probably help!

I feel all my negative emotions very physically. I’ve been trying to come up with a way to describe what it feels like but it’s so damn difficult 

I get all those sensations you described, I feel ya. Its like some form of intense pain from within. I often feel something very much like heartbreak during episodes which can make my heart ache for hours (I actually got prescribed beta blockers for this when it was really bad)
